Base directory for this skill: /Users/kristinarash/.claude/skills/claude-stack-doctor

# Claude Stack Doctor

One command surfaces every known silent-failure class in the automation/memory stack. Run it before debugging anything by hand.

## Quick start

```bash
/opt/homebrew/bin/pwsh -NoProfile -File ~/.claude/skills/claude-stack-doctor/scripts/stack-check.ps1   # Mac
pwsh -NoProfile -File $HOME\.claude\skills\claude-stack-doctor\scripts\stack-check.ps1                 # Windows
```

The same script runs on both machines and picks its checks by OS (see **Two machines** below). On Windows use `pwsh` 7, not `powershell` 5.1, which reports false `memsearch-run` / `backup-cloud-check` failures.

Exit 0 = all clear. Exit 1 = the VERDICT line lists issue codes. Report the findings to the user, then apply the matching fix below.

## Cross-machine handoff (runs on BOTH machines)

`scripts/handoff-check.ps1` is called at the end of `stack-check.ps1`, and it can also be run on its own:

```
powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $HOME\.claude\skills\claude-stack-doctor\scripts\handoff-check.ps1
```

It answers a question nothing else here asked: did state actually make the trip between the two machines? Every other check verifies a component. This verifies the path.

The failure it exists to catch: `daily-backup` pushes `global-memory` nightly and, until 2026-09-12, nothing on the receiving machine ever pulled it. The Windows laptop was found 4 commits behind with every other signal reading healthy, because the backup section measures `ahead` only — which catches a broken push and is blind to a missing pull.

Issue codes:

- `handoff-memory-stale` — `global-memory` is behind origin. This is the serious one: memory written on the other machine is on GitHub and not here, so this session is running on stale context. Fix with `/startup`, or `git -C ~/.claude/global-memory pull --no-rebase`.
- `handoff-behind:<repo>` — config, skills or notes behind origin. Same fix, lower stakes.
- `handoff-unpushed:<repo>` — this machine is more than 3 commits ahead. The other machine cannot see this work; run `/closeout`.
- `handoff-fetch:<repo>` — offline, or GitHub auth has rotted.
- `handoff-repo-gone:<repo>` — the folder is present but is not a git repo. Something replaced a synced repo with a plain folder and its contents are going nowhere.
- A repo absent from the machine entirely is skipped, not failed. `SecondBrain` is Mac-only and its absence on Windows is correct.

The "memory flow" line reports how long since `origin/main` on `global-memory` last advanced. Over 14 days it says so without failing: it cannot distinguish "quiet fortnight" from "the other machine's backup stopped pushing", and a check that cries wolf during the first gets ignored during the second.

## Two machines

`stack-check.ps1` tests `$env:OS -eq 'Windows_NT'` and swaps the machine-specific sections. Everything else (memsearch, flush pipeline, memory repos, cloud receipt, context budget, handoff) is shared.

| Section | Mac | Windows laptop |
|---|---|---|
| Jobs | launchd `com.keystone.*` agents | Task Scheduler: `Backup AI Sessions to Drive`, `DailyGmailDigest`, `CFB-ForecastCaptureReminder` (disabled tasks are skipped) |
| venv | `.venv/bin/python` | `.venv\Scripts\python.exe` |
| memsearch backend | — | Docker Desktop `milvus-standalone` must be `(healthy)` |
| Backup state | `backup-state.json` (daily-backup) | `backup-ai-sessions-state.json` (daily). `Desktop\DEV` itself is a Drive for Desktop synced root; its weekly robocopy task was retired 2026-09-22 (XML in `~/.claude/scripts/retired/`) |
| SecondBrain | checked | skipped, it is Mac-only |

Windows issue codes:
- `task:<name>`: the last run exited non-zero. `3221225786` (0xC000013A, sleep/shutdown kill) only warns; the age check decides whether the job is really behind.
- `task-stale:<name>`, `task-never-run:<name>`, `task-missing:<name>`: the job is behind, has never run, or was deleted. Tasks live under `\Eric\`. Re-run with `Get-ScheduledTask -TaskName '<name>' | Start-ScheduledTask`; a bare `Start-ScheduledTask -TaskName` fails with "cannot find the file specified".
- `task-dual-run:<name>`: a `KeystoneOS-*` task is enabled on Windows. The Mac owns those jobs and the data pulls; disable the Windows copy.
- `milvus-docker` / `milvus-down`: start Docker Desktop; memsearch hooks time out without it.
- `backup-missing:<tag>`, `backup-stale:<tag>`, `backup-error:<tag>`: read `G:\My Drive\00_Primary_Storage_Drive\05_SYSTEMS\AI_Sessions_Backup\<COMPUTERNAME>\_backup_log.txt`. The script silences robocopy, so re-run the robocopy line in the foreground to see which files failed (codes below 8 are success).

On the Windows laptop the weekly run is Task Scheduler task `\Eric\KeystoneOS-StackDoctor` (Mondays 10:30, pwsh 7). It is the one `KeystoneOS-*` task that stays enabled on Windows.

**Mac notes.** Jobs are **launchd user agents** in `~/Library/LaunchAgents/`. The script is PowerShell because `pwsh` runs it natively on both machines. PowerShell on macOS normalises `\` inside a path string to `/`, so the script's mixed separators resolve correctly — verified 2026-08-29. Do not "fix" them.

Useful launchd commands:
```bash
launchctl list | grep keystone                                    # loaded jobs + last exit code
launchctl print gui/$(id -u)/com.keystone.<name>                  # live schedule and state
launchctl bootout  gui/$(id -u)/com.keystone.<name>               # unload
launchctl bootstrap gui/$(id -u) ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.keystone.<name>.plist   # reload
```
Edit a schedule with `/usr/libexec/PlistBuddy -c "Set :StartCalendarInterval:Hour <n>" <plist>`, then bootout + bootstrap. **A plist edit alone does nothing until it is reloaded.**

## Weekly scheduled run

launchd agent `com.keystone.stackdoctor` (Mondays 10:30) runs `scripts/weekly-check.ps1`: the same read-only check, unattended. On failure it appends a one-line summary to `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log` (surfaced at every session start per CLAUDE.md) and the full output is always in `scripts/last-weekly-run.log`. When a session surfaces such an entry, run this skill interactively to diagnose and fix, then clear the entry from `.errors.log`.

**Clearing `.errors.log`:** shell truncation (`: > file`) anywhere under `$HOME` is blocked by dcg rule `core.filesystem:redirect-truncate-root-home`. Use `cp /dev/null <file>`. There is no `truncate` binary on this machine. Archive first — the lines are often live issues, not stale history:
```bash
cp ~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log ~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log.archived-$(date +%Y-%m-%d)
cp /dev/null ~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log
```

## Known failure classes and fixes

These four classes have each bitten more than once (evidence: daily logs 2026-04 → 2026-07). Match the issue code to its fix:

### `task:*` / `task-stale:*` — launchd agent failed or didn't run
1. Read the `action:` line the script printed and run that exact command **manually in a foreground terminal** — launchd discards stdout unless the plist sets `StandardOutPath`; foreground shows the real error.
2. Known root causes: executable referenced without a full path (launchd agents get a minimal PATH — always use full paths like `/opt/homebrew/bin/pwsh`, and set `EnvironmentVariables:PATH` in the plist); a plist edited but never `bootout`+`bootstrap`ed, so the old schedule is still live; the job firing at an hour the required volume is unmounted (see `backup-*`).
3. `launchctl list | grep keystone` shows each job's **last exit code** in column 2. A non-zero there with no output means the script's own log is the only evidence — check `~/.claude/scripts/logs/` and for a `*.log` beside the script.

### `venv-missing` / `venv-broken` — Python venv rot
The script checks `~/.claude/claude-memory-compiler/.venv/bin/python`.
macOS root causes: a Homebrew `python3` major-version bump orphans venvs built against the old interpreter; a `uv` reinstall or relocation breaks tools that hardcode `/Users/kristinarash/.local/bin/uv` (CLAUDE.md forbids relocating it for this reason).
Fix: recreate the venv (`uv sync` in the project, or `python3 -m venv .venv` + reinstall from its pyproject), then run the dependent agent once by hand to confirm.
*History (Windows box, retired 2026-08-14): Python Install Manager migrations deleted `C:\Python31x` twice, silently killing morning-briefing for 6 days. The lesson transfers — an interpreter move breaks every venv built on it — the paths do not.*

### `memsearch-path` / `memsearch-run` — memsearch CLI broken
memsearch is a **uv tool** on this machine: binary at `/Users/kristinarash/.local/bin/memsearch`, environment at `/Users/kristinarash/.local/share/uv/tools/memsearch/`.
- Not on PATH or the binary errors → reinstall with `uv tool install --force memsearch`, not pip.
- Import failures inside the tool env (e.g. `onnxruntime`) are testable directly:
  `/Users/kristinarash/.local/share/uv/tools/memsearch/bin/python -c "import onnxruntime; print(onnxruntime.__version__)"`
- **After ANY reinstall/upgrade of memsearch the local flush patch is stripped.** Re-apply it (notes in `~/.claude/claude-memory-compiler/`), then confirm `.errors.log` stays empty for a session.
- `INDEX full set: Indexed 0 chunks` in the nightly log is **usually not an indexer fault** — it means nothing new arrived. Check `flush-stale` first; a dead flush pipeline starves the indexer and looks identical (confirmed 2026-08-29).

### `recall-coverage` / `recall-regress` — memory search can't find what it should
- `recall-coverage`: a root in `KeystoneOS/data/memory-index-paths.json` doesn't exist on this machine, so it is never indexed (the hooks skip missing roots; `memsearch-sync.js` lists them at the top of `.memsearch-index.log`). Paths take `{HOME}`, `{DEV}` and `{VAULT}`; a machine-specific location needs a token, not a hardcoded path. The other machine's Tier A slug is the one expected miss.
- `recall-regress`: hit@5 fell by 2+ between this machine's last two runs of a backend in `~/.claude/audits/recall-eval/ledger.md`.
- **The eval:** `python ~/.claude/audits/recall-eval/recall-eval.py --label "<model or change>"` (add `--backends fts5,rg` when Docker is down or RAM is short). Known-answer cases live in `questions.jsonl`. Rerun after a model change, a memsearch/context-mode upgrade, or any edit to the index paths. **Scheduled (Windows):** Task Scheduler `\Eric\memsearch-drain-weekly` (Sundays 02:00) runs reindex → eval (all four backends, label `weekly`) → `audits/recall-eval/after-run.ps1`, which commits+pushes the results, writes `LATEST.md`, and only on a problem appends to `.errors.log`. Spec and decision rule: `~/.claude/audits/2026-09-30-memory-infra-audit.md` §6.

### `errors-log` / `flush-stale` / `flush-error` / `flush-missing` — memory pipeline
- `.errors.log` non-empty → read the entries **before clearing**; they are frequently live unresolved issues rather than stale history. Common causes: the stripped memsearch flush patch (above), or an Agent SDK timeout ("Control request timeout: initialize" — transient, but recurring daily means the hook environment is broken).
- `last-flush.json` stale >48h → check `~/.claude/claude-memory-compiler/scripts/flush.log` tail for the real error. `last-flush.json` is written by `flush.py` **only on success**, so a stale timestamp means flushes are dying, not that the hook never fired.
- **Stranded context files are the tell.** `session-end.py` writes `scripts/session-flush-<session>-<stamp>.md` then spawns `flush.py`, which **deletes that file on success**. So every leftover `session-flush-*.md` in `~/.claude/claude-memory-compiler/scripts/` is a flush that died, and its date maps to a missing `daily/<date>.md`.
  Recover one by re-running it by hand (~1 min, writes into the daily log):
  ```bash
  /Users/kristinarash/.local/bin/uv run --directory ~/.claude/claude-memory-compiler \
    python ~/.claude/claude-memory-compiler/scripts/flush.py <context-file> <session-id>
  ```
  Success looks like `Result: FLUSH_OK` + `Flush complete` in `flush.log`.
- No `SessionEnd fired` lines in `flush.log` for days, yet the hook works when run by hand → sessions are being closed rather than exited cleanly. Self-verifying: end one session normally and re-check the tail.
- FLUSH_ERROR in dailies → same investigation; `flush.log` is ground truth.

### `backup-*` — daily backup rot
launchd agent `com.keystone.dailybackup` (**21:00 daily** since 2026-09-24; 09:00 from 2026-08-29) runs `~/.claude/scripts/daily-backup.ps1`: auto-commits+pushes the memory repos (SecondBrain, dotclaude, claude-skills, claude-global-memory), **rsync**-snapshots `~/.claude/projects`, `~/.codex`, `~/.gemini` and non-repo DEV folders to Google Drive at `~/Library/CloudStorage/GoogleDrive-eric.rash11@gmail.com/My Drive/…`, captures the same set to the **CRASHBOX SSD** at `/Volumes/CRASHBOX/AssistantBackup/` when it is mounted, runs an uncapped full memsearch reindex, and resets the hook's timeout-streak counter. Restore procedure: `~/.claude/RESTORE.md`.

**The SSD layer's signature failure — a clean exit code is not evidence.** If CRASHBOX is unmounted the run logs `TARGET SSD … NOT MOUNTED … SKIPPED` and still ends `OK (0 errors)`. The schedule moved 00:30 → 09:00 on 2026-08-29 precisely because the drive was never attached at 00:30. **Verify an SSD capture only by a fresh receipt** at `/Volumes/CRASHBOX/AssistantBackup/_receipts/run-*.txt`. Never by directory mtimes (`rsync -a` preserves source mtimes, and a parent dir's mtime moves only when an entry is added or removed — top-level SSD dirs legitimately show weeks-old dates after a perfect capture) and never by `du`. `-DryRun` runs `rsync -n` and proves nothing about writes.
- `backup-missing` / `backup-stale` → job didn't run; re-run foreground (~6 min): `/opt/homebrew/bin/pwsh -File ~/.claude/scripts/daily-backup.ps1`. There is no SSD-only switch, and one should not be added.
- `backup-error` → read `~/.claude/scripts/logs/daily-backup.log`; a `repo-diverged:*` entry means a memory repo has both remote and local changes — reconcile manually (the script refuses to merge from automation).
- `backup-repo-drift:*` → pushes failing (>3 unpushed commits); usually gh/git auth rot — run `gh auth status`.
- `backup-cloud-*` → the Drive-API heartbeat (gws CLI queries RESTORE.md's cloud modifiedTime). `-check` = gws auth rot; re-auth needs explicit full scope URLs: `gws auth login --scopes "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive,https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar.readonly"` (the `-s drive` shorthand silently grants NO scopes, v0.22.5 bug). After re-auth delete `~/.config/gws/token_cache.json` or it serves the stale token. The login is interactive — Eric must run it himself via `!` while at the machine, then open the printed URL directly; terminal copy/paste truncates it at line-wrap. `-stale`/`-missing` = files reach the local CloudStorage cache but Google Drive for Desktop isn't syncing — check that Google Drive is running and signed in.
- Drive is a **FUSE CloudStorage mount**: it rounds mtimes it did not write, so `rsync -a` re-sends identical files forever. Use `--modify-window=5`; never `--size-only`.

## Not covered by the script (check manually if symptoms point there)

- **MCP/plugin auth rot** (9 manual fix-it sessions on record): run `claude doctor` / `claude mcp list` and re-auth any claude.ai connectors showing failures (Supabase, Vercel, Google Calendar have all rotted before).
- **Catapult OpenField token expiry**: see the auth section of `pp-catapult-openfield-connect`.

## Gotchas

- **`flush.py` always writes into *today's* daily log.** Recovering a weeks-old stranded `session-flush-*.md` files old facts under today's date, and the compiler then treats them as current. Recover only recent ones. Move old ones to `scripts/_stranded-archive/` so a file left in `scripts/` still means a flush that died recently (3 files from June archived 2026-09-22).
- **Drive's `name contains` is token matching, not substring.** The cloud check's `run-2` query also returned `jev_run2.jsonl`, so results are filtered to `run-*.txt` on the client.
- **Desktop Commander MCP times out at session start on Windows.** It starts through `npx -y …@latest`, which checks the npm registry every time: 23s alone, 30–46s alongside the other servers, against a 30s default. `MCP_TIMEOUT=90000` in `~/.claude/settings.json` `env` fixes it (set 2026-09-22). If it times out again, raise the timeout; don't edit the synced plugin's `plugin.json`, which is re-synced on the next launch.
- **Stale `.git/worktrees/<name>` dirs that `git worktree prune` can't delete ("Permission denied") are not locked.** Their empty `logs`/`refs` subfolders are read-only; `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force <dir>` clears them (2026-09-22, with Drive quit and prune still failing).
- **`flush.log` "SKIP: transcript missing" is not a fault.** It comes from sessions that were opened and closed before any message was sent, so there is nothing to flush.

## Rules

- Read-only by default: the script never mutates state. Fixes are applied by you, deliberately, after reporting findings.
- Don't assume the obvious culprit — a signal that pattern-matches a known failure may have a different cause (lesson: 6/25 Milvus/ETIMEDOUT misdiagnosis). Confirm with the foreground re-run before fixing.
- When a fix is applied, re-run the script to verify the issue code clears, and note the incident in memory if it's a new failure class.

---
name: memsearch-index-is-destructive
description: "`memsearch index <paths>` deletes every indexed source outside the given paths — never run it with a partial or test path set; plus the 2026-10-07 Windows failure causes"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 4f57cc78-0bf6-4202-bd61-8f428a3c6dca
  modified: 2026-10-07T22:05:05.745Z
---

`memsearch index <paths>` is **never read-only**. It reconciles the collection against
the path set it is given and deletes every indexed source not under those paths
(core.py `index()` → store.py delete). An empty or partial path set wipes the rest.

On 2026-10-07 a diagnostic run against an empty temp dir deleted ~12,900 of ~31,000
vectors before it was stopped. Recovery: a full re-index over all 13 paths in
`KeystoneOS/data/memory-index-paths.json`, which takes hours on Windows (~3 s/chunk).
`memsearch stats` counts tombstones until compaction, so use `count(*)` for live rows.

**Why:** a "just timing it" run silently destroyed 40% of the index.
**How to apply:** never pass a test or partial path set to `memsearch index`. To time
indexing, use a throwaway collection or time `memsearch search`. For a catch-up run,
use `~/.claude/scripts/memsearch-drain.ps1`: it resolves the full path set and holds
the hook's lock.

Windows failure causes found the same day:
- **10-06 "Milvus unreachable":** Docker Desktop's vpnkit port forward to
  milvus-standalone flapped after days of uptime through Modern Standby. Milvus itself
  never restarted. A Docker restart cleared it.
- **10-07 ETIMEDOUT ×9:** low free RAM (1–2 GB) slowed indexing to ~1.2 s/chunk, so the
  hook's 600s cap killed every run partway. The cap was raised to 3h on 2026-10-07.
  The streak never resets on Windows because no nightly reindex runs there.

Related: [[memsearch-hook-timeout-cap]], [[automation-cadence]].
---

/Users/kristinarash/.claude/scripts/memsearch-drain.ps1
# memsearch-drain.ps1 -- one-off foreground catch-up of the memsearch backlog.
#
# Why (2026-09-28, Windows laptop): ~10,100 chunks were never indexed. The
# SessionEnd hook caps each run at 600s and this CPU embeds ~5 s/chunk with
# bge-m3, so every run was killed after ~110 chunks and the next session end
# restarted it -- 2.5-3 GB of RAM all day. This runs the same incremental
# index with no cap, once, then gets out of the way.
#
# Coordination: holds ~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.memsearch-index.lock
# with THIS process's PID for the whole run (the hook skips while the owner is
# alive), and refreshes .memsearch-last-run so the hook's 30-min cooldown is in
# force when it finishes. Runs BelowNormal so interactive work keeps the CPU.
# batch_size comes from ~/.memsearch/config.toml (8 since 2026-09-28).

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$T       = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE '.claude\global-memory\transcripts'
$lock    = Join-Path $T '.memsearch-index.lock'
$lastRun = Join-Path $T '.memsearch-last-run'
$streak  = Join-Path $T '.memsearch-timeout-streak'
$log     = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE '.claude\scripts\logs\memsearch-drain.log'
$exe     = Join-Path $env:APPDATA 'Python\Python314\Scripts\memsearch.exe'
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force (Split-Path $log) | Out-Null
function Log($m) { Add-Content -LiteralPath $log -Value "[$((Get-Date).ToString('s'))] $m" }

# Same path source as memsearch-sync.js.
$dev  = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE 'Desktop\DEV'
$vault = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE 'Desktop\SecondBrain'   # {VAULT}; this script is Windows-only
$cfg  = Get-Content -Raw (Join-Path $dev 'KeystoneOS\data\memory-index-paths.json') | ConvertFrom-Json
$paths = @($cfg.paths | ForEach-Object {
    ($_ -replace '\{HOME\}', $env:USERPROFILE -replace '\{DEV\}', $dev -replace '\{VAULT\}', $vault) -replace '/', '\'
} | Where-Object { Test-Path -LiteralPath $_ })

# Take the lock atomically; wait up to 20 min for a live hook run to finish.
$deadline = (Get-Date).AddMinutes(20)
while ($true) {
    try {
        $fs = [IO.File]::Open($lock, [IO.FileMode]::CreateNew); $fs.Close()
